propositions.text: The market is structurally short-term gas due to buying pressure from California entities.
Williams, Calpine, and Dynegy are unconcerned about short-term gas prices between 450 and 525.
Term gas prices will not decline short term unless front prices drop to the 400s, triggering producers to hedge.
El Paso and the speaker's company are seeking fixed price LNG contracts for 250,000 MMBtu/day over 10 years.
The sender of the email is Jennifer Fraser, and her phone number is 713-853-4759.
Trading prices for April to October are at 540, while the estimated real worth is 500.
Trading prices for November to March are at 547, while the estimated real worth is 375.
Trading price for calendar year 2 is 491, while the estimated real worth is 400.
Trading price for calendar year 3 is 460, while the estimated real worth is 325.
The bearishness of the market increases the further out the delivery time goes in these prices and worth assessments.
The current game or market strategy is not sell and hold, although it will be soon.
The current market focus is on predicting where prices will be tomorrow, next week, and next month.
The market is structurally short term gas due to demand from California buyers.
California is buying power, and market participants Williams, Calpine, and Dynegy do not consider gas cost variations in levels such as 450, 475, 500, or 525 as important.
Short term gas prices will not go down unless the front month prices enter the 400's range and cause some producers to start hedging.
An alternative condition for term prices to decrease in the short term is if the speaker or El Paso can find fixed price LNG to the tune of 250,000 a day for 10 years.
